title: A fresh clone says "not initialized" instead of fetching the data ref
body:
git clone only fetches refs/heads/*, so a clone of a repository that ran foam init elsewhere has no refs/foam/data. The first foam command there prints "foam is not initialized here" and nothing else, and the person does not learn that foam init in the clone would fetch the ref from origin and set up sync (tests/cli.rs sync_moves_data_between_clones_and_merges_it covers that path, and the README's storage and sync section states it).

Two fixes, either or both:

1. Say what to do. When the local ref is missing and the repository has an origin, the error becomes: foam is not initialized here; run foam init to fetch refs/foam/data from origin, or to start fresh. No network call, no behaviour change.

2. Adopt on first use. A command that finds no local ref but has an origin runs ls-remote, and if the data ref is there, fetches it and sets up sync before doing its own work. One round trip on the first command in every uninitialized clone. prime --hook-json stays exempt: it runs in every repository at session start, foam or not.

Related: the ref only reaches the remote through the pre-push hook, so a repository never pushed after foam init has nothing for a clone to fetch. When ls-remote finds no data ref, the message could say that the origin has none yet and that foam sync on the original machine sends it.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/6de6737a
notes.text:
What the gap looks like in practice, from a repo that ran foam init before it had a remote:

The first machine never pushed the ref. foam init installs the fetch refspec and the pre-push hook only if origin exists when it runs, so a remote added afterwards gets neither, git push reports everything up to date, and only foam doctor says anything is missing. The clone's foam init then found no data ref on origin, started a fresh empty root, and added the refspec anyway. A configured refspec whose source ref does not exist on the remote is fatal to every fetch, so git pull in the clone died with: couldn't find remote ref refs/foam/data.

Two more gaps to close alongside the error message:

1. Do not install the refspec before the remote has the ref, or use a glob form, which git skips when nothing matches. Either way git pull must keep working in a clone whose origin has no data yet.

2. Say so when init runs without a remote: sync is not set up, and foam sync --setup does it once origin exists. foam sync could also install the refspec and hook on its own first run instead of needing --setup.

Recovery, for the record: foam sync --setup on the first machine, then foam sync in the clone; the two roots merge (tests/cli.rs two_clones_that_both_ran_init_still_merge).

notes.author: Jack Roddy/6de6737a
notes.text: Fixed in the working tree on dev. The refspec is now added only when the remote has the ref: init adds it after fetching, sync adds it after a successful push or when ls-remote finds it. sync also installs the hook on every run, so --setup only adds the advice for a hook it cannot install. init prints a line when origin has no ref yet and when there is no remote. The error names foam init. Adopt-on-first-use was not done: the message is enough and it would cost a round trip on every uninitialized command.
